name: VictoriaMetrics
tagline: Resource-frugal, Prometheus-compatible metrics database, run as a single binary or a sharded cluster.
description: VictoriaMetrics is a time-series database and monitoring stack built to do more per CPU core and per gigabyte of disk than other Prometheus-ecosystem backends. It ingests Prometheus remote write, InfluxDB line protocol, Graphite, OpenTSDB, Datadog and OpenTelemetry, and answers PromQL plus its superset MetricsQL. The single-node binary covers most teams; the cluster version splits vminsert, vmstorage and vmselect for horizontal scale and multi-tenancy, without needing Kafka or object storage. Enterprise adds downsampling, per-series retention filters and automated backups, and VictoriaMetrics Cloud is the vendor's managed service.

pricing.notes: Open-source single-node and cluster are free; Enterprise is a subscription; VictoriaMetrics Cloud is usage-based.

scale.notes: Cluster shards series across vmstorage nodes with optional replication; cross-region setups rely on vmagent dual-writes.

strengths: Very low RAM and disk per active series keeps hardware bills small
Drop-in Prometheus remote-write target with PromQL-compatible MetricsQL
One binary accepts Prometheus, Influx, Graphite, OpenTSDB, Datadog and OTLP ingestion
Cluster mode scales on plain disks with no Kafka, ZooKeeper or object-store dependency
Apache-2.0 including multi-tenancy in the open-source cluster
weaknesses: No built-in cross-region replication; durability relies on replicationFactor or vmagent dual-writes
Downsampling and retention filters are Enterprise-only
MetricsQL differs from PromQL in edge cases, which can surprise when switching back
Uses block storage rather than object storage, so very long retention costs more than S3-backed systems
useCases: Kubernetes monitoring with vmagent and the operator
Consolidating Graphite, Influx and Prometheus metrics in one store
Cutting cost when moving off SaaS metrics
